notes: CRITICAL: The 'spawned knowledge-researcher subagent' assertion has NEVER passed across either iteration for EITHER version (0/4 runs). Neither skill version successfully delegates to the researcher agent. This assertion is non-discriminating and likely reflects a fundamental behavior — subagents inside subagents may not work reliably.

Eval 1 critical-patterns.md: The hybrid skill DID check critical-patterns.md per its transcript, but the grader judged based on the output response.md which didn't mention it (since no patterns matched). This is an assertion design issue — checking but not reporting is correct behavior when no patterns match.
The hybrid version was consistently faster: 77s vs 149s on eval 1, 98s vs 118s on eval 3. Eval 2 was slower (150s vs 120s).
vault-recommender was correctly NOT used in any eval — all three had sufficient grep results. Need a test case with a conceptual query that grep handles poorly to test this capability.

Across both iterations (4 total runs), the old procedural version averages 93.3% pass rate vs 83.3-86.7% for prompt-object variants. The gap is entirely in eval 1 where procedural mandates produce more transparent outputs.
